I've been farming this land for 40 years. My hands know this soil. I grow stevia because the buyers from the processing plant in the county come and collect it, and the price is stable enough. I have 5.5 mu, all of it in stevia — that's what I know, that's what my family depends on.

In spring, after the Qingming festival when the ground warms up, I hire my neighbor's rotary tiller to turn the soil. I always do this — it breaks up the clods, mixes in the fertilizer I spread beforehand. I use compound fertilizer at the base, then come back with urea when the plants are growing strong. Not too much nitrogen — I learned that lesson years ago, the leaves get big but the buyers complain the quality is off.

I plant stevia seedlings I buy from the supply cooperative. The improved ones root better and give more leaves than the old stock. I put them all 5.5 mu into stevia — no reason to change. The well is reliable, so I irrigate when the weather gets dry, which in Quzhou is often. I count maybe 10 times through the season. I spray for pests — aphids mostly, sometimes whitefly — two or three times, when I see the problem starting, not before.

I harvest twice before the frost comes, cutting before the flowers open because that's when the leaves are best.
